title: Trois mois sur un bateau  (Three Months on a Boat)

segments.t: Then Laura found out that Mathias had given the very same script to her mother, Nathalie Baye: the director wants them both, to play a mother and her daughter. Laura loves the script. The problem is somewhere else, and she's about to tell Gabriel where. First, the French. Don't try to hold on to every word; just listen to how they sound.
Quoi? Tu n'aimes pas le scénario?
Si, je l'adore.
Mais trois mois de tournage, sur un bateau, en pleine mer!
Je ne peux pas supporter ça.
Je connais un excellent acupuncteur contre le mal de mer.
Non. Je parle de ma mère.
Trois mois! Tu connais un acupuncteur pour ça?
Mais tu étais contente!
Je l'aime.
Mais je ne peux pas rester avec elle sur un bateau!
Attends. Parle d'abord à Akerfelt.
Après, tu vas voir les choses différemment.
Si elle est un génie, ce sera encore plus dur de refuser.
Laura, tu ne peux pas refuser!
Bon. Je vais lui parler.
Let's go through it gently. Gabriel picks up and immediately fears the worst.
Quoi?
'What?' Short and blunt, the everyday way to react to a surprise.
Tu n'aimes pas le scénario?
'Don't you like the script?' The negative goes around the verb for 'like'; before a vowel the first little word shrinks. Now listen carefully to the first word of Laura's answer.
Si, je l'adore.

'Yes, I love it.' That's the special yes again, the one you use to contradict a negative question. Gabriel asked 'don't you like it?', so a plain yes would sound wrong. And the little word for 'it' sits before the verb.
Mais trois mois de tournage, sur un bateau, en pleine mer!
'But three months of shooting, on a boat, out at sea!' Literally 'in full sea'. You can hear she isn't thrilled.
Je ne peux pas supporter ça.
'I can't stand that.' This everyday French sentence pairs 'I' with 'that'.
Je connais un excellent acupuncteur contre le mal de mer.
'I know an excellent acupuncturist for seasickness.' Literally 'against the sickness of the sea'. Gabriel, ever helpful, has completely misunderstood.
Non. Je parle de ma mère.
'No. I'm talking about my mother.' In French you 'talk of' something. And the word for 'my' is feminine here, to go with 'mother'.
Trois mois! Tu connais un acupuncteur pour ça?
'Three months! Do you know an acupuncturist for that?' She throws his own words back at him.
Mais tu étais contente!
'But you were happy!' The verb 'to be' in the form for describing how things were. And 'happy' has a feminine ending for Laura.
Mais je ne peux pas rester avec elle sur un bateau!
'But I cannot stay with her on a boat!' Same verb as 'like', and once more the little object word goes before the verb. Here it means 'her'.
Mais je ne peux pas être avec elle sur un bateau, jour et nuit!
'But I can't be with her on a boat, day and night!' The word for 'her' after 'with' is the same as the word for 'she'.
Attends.
'Wait.' A casual command; you'll hear it all the time.
Parle d'abord à Akerfelt.
'Talk to Akerfelt first.' The phrase in the middle means 'first of all'. Gabriel thinks the director will win her over.
Après, tu vas voir les choses différemment.
'Afterwards, you'll see things differently.' The verb 'to go' plus 'see' talks about the near future: you are going to see.
Si elle est un génie, ce sera encore plus dur de refuser.
'If she's a genius, it'll be even harder to say no.' That's the real future tense: 'it will be'. And 'even more hard' is how French says 'even harder'. Laura is afraid of liking it too much.
Laura, tu ne peux pas refuser!
'Laura, you can't say no!' The agent's cry from the heart. A film with mother and daughter would be a big deal for the agency.
Bon. Je vais lui parler.
'Okay. I'll talk to her.' Near future again, and that small word before the verb means 'to her'. For now, Laura gives in. Good. Let's listen to the whole call once more.
Quoi? Tu n'aimes pas le scénario?
Si, je l'adore.
Mais trois mois de tournage, sur un bateau, en pleine mer!
Je ne peux pas supporter ça.
Je connais un excellent acupuncteur contre le mal de mer.
Non. Je parle de ma mère.
Trois mois! Tu connais un acupuncteur pour ça?
Mais tu étais contente!
Je l'aime.
Mais je ne peux pas rester avec elle sur un bateau!
Attends. Parle d'abord à Akerfelt.
Après, tu vas voir les choses différemment.
Si elle est un génie, ce sera encore plus dur de refuser.
Laura, tu ne peux pas refuser!
Bon. Je vais lui parler.
Short and sweet, and you followed all of it. Listen out for that special yes when people answer a negative question. See you next time!
Salut, Gabriel!
